subject: Mathematics
chapter_title: A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines
summary: Discovery of triangles formed by three mutually non-concurrent intersecting lines, angle sum property ($180^\circ$), exterior angle property, and triangle inequality theorem.

theory_summary.topic: Angle Sum Property of a Triangle
theory_summary.content: The sum of all three interior angles of any triangle is always $180^\circ$: $\angle A + \angle B + \angle C = 180^\circ$.
An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its two interior opposite angles: $\angle \text{ext} = \angle 1 + \angle 2$.
The sum of any two sides of a triangle is strictly greater than the third side: $a + b > c$.

questions.question: The three angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2 : 3 : 5$. What is the measure of the largest angle?
questions.explanation: Let angles be $2x, 3x, 5x$. $2x + 3x + 5x = 180^\circ \implies 10x = 180^\circ \implies x = 18^\circ$. Largest angle $= 5 \times 18^\circ = 90^\circ$.

questions.question: An exterior angle of a triangle measures $115^\circ$ and one of its interior opposite angles is $45^\circ$. What is the other interior opposite angle?
questions.explanation: Exterior angle = sum of interior opposite angles: $115^\circ = 45^\circ + x \implies x = 115^\circ - 45^\circ = 70^\circ$.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of lengths CANNOT form a triangle?
questions.explanation: By triangle inequality, the sum of any two sides must be strictly greater than the third side: $2 + 5 = 7 < 8$, so no triangle can be formed.

questions.question: The line segment joining a vertex of a triangle to the midpoint of its opposite side is called a _______.
questions.explanation: Every triangle has three medians which intersect at a single point called the centroid.

questions.question: In an equilateral triangle, each interior angle measures $60^\circ$. (True/False)
questions.explanation: Since all three angles are equal: $\frac{180^\circ}{3} = 60^\circ$.

questions.question: $ABCD$ is a quadrilateral. Prove that $AB + BC + CD + DA > AC + BD$.
questions.answer:
• **Proof**:
  1. Consider $\triangle ABC$. By the triangle inequality theorem (sum of two sides > third side):
     $$AB + BC > AC \quad \text{--- (1)}$$
  2. In $\triangle ADC$:
     $$AD + CD > AC \quad \text{--- (2)}$$
  3. In $\triangle ABD$:
     $$AB + DA > BD \quad \text{--- (3)}$$
  4. In $\triangle BCD$:
     $$BC + CD > BD \quad \text{--- (4)}$$
  5. Adding inequalities (1), (2), (3), and (4):
     $$(AB + BC) + (AD + CD) + (AB + DA) + (BC + CD) > AC + AC + BD + BD$$
     $$2AB + 2BC + 2CD + 2DA > 2AC + 2BD$$
     $$2(AB + BC + CD + DA) > 2(AC + BD)$$
  6. Dividing both sides by 2:
     $$\mathbf{AB + BC + CD + DA > AC + BD}$$
  Hence proved.
questions.explanation: Classic quadrilateral perimeter versus diagonals inequality proof.
